senses.definition_en: anecdote

examples.english: The word beat out five other shortlisted candidates, including ‘lore’, which means a set of (supposed) facts, background information and anecdotes necessary to fully understand something; ‘romantasy’, an acronym for literature that combines elements of romantic fiction and fantasy; and ‘slop’, which refers to low-quality content generated by artificial intelligence.
examples.ref: 2024 December 2, Rosa Rahimi, “La palabra del año de Oxford es una condición moderna que nos resulta familiar a la mayoría de nosotros”, in CNN en Español:
examples.text: La palabra superó a otras cinco candidatas preseleccionadas, que incluían “lore”, que significa un conjunto de (supuestos) hechos, información de fondo y anécdotas necesarias para comprender algo por completo; “romantasy”, un acrónimo para literatura que combina elementos de ficción romántica y fantasía; y “slop”, que se refiere a contenido de baja calidad generado por inteligencia artificial.
examples.translation: The word beat out five other shortlisted candidates, including ‘lore’, which means a set of (supposed) facts, background information and anecdotes necessary to fully understand something; ‘romantasy’, an acronym for literature that combines elements of romantic fiction and fantasy; and ‘slop’, which refers to low-quality content generated by artificial intelligence.

examples.english: The anecdote is relevant because, first, it illustrates the ideological climate surrounding the study of rhetoric, and second, it points out how in grammar class students used to study texts that were generally recommended for the rhetoric course.
examples.ref: 1989, Osario Romero, Ignacio, Conquistar el eco. La paradoja de la conciencia criolla, page 199:
examples.text: La anécdota viene a cuento porque, primero, ilustra el clima ideológico del estudio de la retórica y, segundo, señala cómo en la clase de gramática solían estudiarse textos que, generalmente, eran recomendados para el curso de retórica.
examples.translation: The anecdote is relevant because, first, it illustrates the ideological climate surrounding the study of rhetoric, and second, it points out how in grammar class students used to study texts that were generally recommended for the rhetoric course.

senses.definition_en: a protest against Nicolás Maduro

examples.english: In February 2014 it was the epicentre of the social protests, called guarimbas, against the Nicolás Maduro government that had been extending to other Venezuelan cities for three months and keeping the governance of the country in check.
examples.ref: 2015 November 16, Ewald Scharfenberg, “Táchira, la vida en estado de excepción”, in El País:
examples.text: En febrero de 2014 fue el epicentro de las protestas sociales, llamadas guarimbas, contra el Gobierno de Nicolás Maduro que durante tres meses se extendieron a otras ciudades venezolanas y pusieron en jaque la gobernabilidad del país.
examples.translation: In February 2014 it was the epicentre of the social protests, called guarimbas, against the Nicolás Maduro government that had been extending to other Venezuelan cities for three months and keeping the governance of the country in check.

examples.english: The word guarimba is related to the refuge or hiding place that protects children playing in groups from the elements, in recent years it refers to a style of protest.
examples.ref: 2017 June 13, “Sobre búnkers y trincheras: el papel de los edificios en las guarimbas”, in Misión Verdad, archived from the original on 18 Jan 2018:
examples.text: La palabra guarimba está relacionada con el refugio o escondite que salva de quedar fuera a los niños o adolescentes que juegan en grupos, en los últimos años se refiere a un estilo de protesta.
examples.translation: The word guarimba is related to the refuge or hiding place that protects children playing in groups from the elements, in recent years it refers to a style of protest.

senses.definition_en: a street blockade used in protest against the government, often set on fire

examples.english: ...this consists of blockades of streets and main avenues, with rubbish, objects, and any item that will serve to stop movement. In Venezuela this has a key name: "guarimba".
examples.ref: 2014 February 20, Vladimir Hernández, “Caracas vivió una intensa noche de disturbios”, in BBC Mundo:
examples.text: ...consistía en bloquear en acciones relámpago calles o avenidas neurálgicas, con basura, objetos o cualquier cosa que sirva para detener el tránsito. En Venezuela eso tiene un nombre clave: "guarimba".
examples.translation: ...this consists of blockades of streets and main avenues, with rubbish, objects, and any item that will serve to stop movement. In Venezuela this has a key name: "guarimba".

glosses: a street blockade used in protest against the government, often set on fire
